title: Fabric vs Power BI
changes: Removed unsupported most-searched hook and no-refresh absolute. Direct Lake refreshes metadata; this isn't a live Fabric demo.

beats.text: Microsoft Fabric versus Power BI? Power BI is already inside Fabric.
Power BI handles reports. Fabric covers the workflow around those reports.
Getting data in. Storing it. Transforming it. Then serving the result.
OneLake gives those workloads a shared, logical data lake.
Direct Lake can read Delta tables without importing an entire copy into the model.
A Direct Lake refresh still exists. It updates metadata, rather than copying the whole dataset.
Already know Power BI? Keep it. Add SQL, a lakehouse, and an ingestion pipeline.
Start with one end to end workflow. Follow the data into the report.

title: The free DP-700 preparation path
changes: Replaced expired voucher promotion and unverified historical frequency with currently documented preparation resources. No promise of future vouchers.

beats.text: Want to prepare for DP seven hundred without buying a course? Start with Microsoft's own resources.
First, open the Fabric Data Engineer certification page on Microsoft Learn.
Use the study guide to see the skills the exam measures.
Then work through the free, self paced learning material linked from that page.
Use the free practice assessment to find the areas you still need to study.
Try the exam sandbox so the interface is familiar before exam day.
Preparation is free. An exam booking is a separate purchase unless you have a valid offer.
Save the official certification page. Check any voucher's eligibility and deadline before relying on it.

title: The Fabric workflow beyond charts
changes: Removed predictions about all analysts, one-bill oversimplification, hiring guarantees and universal job-posting claims.

beats.text: If you already build Power BI reports, learn what happens before the chart.
Fabric brings ingestion, engineering, storage, analytics and reporting into one platform.
Start with a lakehouse. Understand where the data lands and how its tables are organized.
Then trace an ingestion pipeline. What arrives, what changes, and what happens when a run fails?
Keep SQL and Power BI. Add the shared data layer underneath them.
Fabric data agents can turn questions into queries against supported data sources.
That makes a clean model and clear permissions useful beyond the report itself.
Build one small workflow from source to report. Explain each step and show its output.

title: The Direct Lake interview question
changes: Quiz is an original adaptation; the reference demonstrates SQL masking. Replaced blanket security/fallback claims with documented Direct Lake distinctions.

beats.text: A Fabric interview question. Your sales data is stored as Delta tables in OneLake.
You want import style query performance without copying the entire dataset into the model.
Which storage mode fits? Import? Direct Query? Or Direct Lake?
Pause here and choose your answer.
Direct Lake. It loads the columns needed for queries from Delta tables in OneLake.
A refresh updates metadata. It does not import the entire dataset again.
Here is the detail to check. Direct Lake on SQL can fall back to Direct Query.
Direct Lake on OneLake does not use that fallback. Their security behavior differs too.
Read the comparison before choosing a mode. The correct design depends on the source and permissions.

title: Ask Fabric data questions in plain English
changes: Removed unsupported fixed cost, language and trial absolutes. Uses official documentation captures; no fabricated execution or answer.

beats.text: Your Power BI semantic model can also be a source for a Fabric data agent.
Microsoft's documented setup starts by creating the agent and choosing its data sources.
You can add up to five supported sources in one agent.
Select the tables it should use. Give columns and tables descriptive names.
Then ask a concrete question. For example, what were total sales in California in twenty twenty three?
The agent can generate SQL, DAX or KQL, depending on the data source.
It uses your data access permissions. Clear descriptions and a clean model help it choose the right query.
Before a real demo, check capacity prerequisites, permissions, and the generated query against a known answer.

title: Three free Fabric learning resources
changes: Removed promise of identical exam wording/difficulty and stale trial exclusions. Trial availability remains subject to Microsoft's eligibility rules.

beats.text: Three free Microsoft resources for learning Fabric. Save these official pages.
One. A Fabric trial gives eligible users sixty days to explore the platform.
Use it to practice lakehouses, ingestion and reporting. Check the current trial limits before you start.
Two. The DP seven hundred practice assessment is available free on Microsoft Learn.
Use the feedback to find gaps. It is a study tool, not a guarantee of an exam result.
Three. The exam sandbox lets you explore the exam interface before booking your test.
Start with the certification page and follow its official links. Keep the resources together for your next study session.

title: Claude dashboards: connect, ask, inspect
changes: Verified first-party feature text via Firecrawl. Original source cards replace unlicensed creator footage. Not a recorded product execution; omitted categorical Power BI export exclusion.

beats.text: Claude Dashboards can connect to Databricks and build a dashboard from a question.
Anthropic announced it on October eighth. The announcement describes a beta on paid plans.
Step one. Connect a supported data platform, such as Databricks, Snowflake or Big Query.
Step two. Ask a specific question in plain English, like this week's signups compared with last month's.
Claude retrieves the data and builds the dashboard. This is a source based walkthrough of the announced feature.
Step three. Inspect the answer. The announcement says you can click a number to see its query.
Each chart also shows when its data was last refreshed.
Enterprise admins must enable the feature. Check access and verify the query before sharing the result.

title: A year of New York's 311 requests
changes: Recomputed results through NYC's public API. Removed claim of a Fabric execution; chart is original and backed by saved query responses. Date range is Oct 1 2025 through Sep 30 2026.

beats.text: I queried a year of New York's three one one requests. Almost four million records.
The window is October first, twenty twenty five, through September thirtieth, twenty twenty six.
The biggest category is illegal parking. Six hundred eleven thousand, two hundred eighty two requests.
Residential noise is next, with more than four hundred thirty two thousand requests.
Those residential noise requests peak in the ten p m hour. Sunday is the busiest day.
Heat and hot water requests show a different pattern. January is far busier than August.
At the other end of the list, exactly one request is filed under trapping pigeon.
These are request counts, not unique incidents. The queries and results are saved so you can reproduce the charts.

title: Before you pause Fabric capacity
changes: Kept reservation and smoothed-usage caveats; clarified that pausing does not stop the reservation charge. Original reference is a cumulative list, not a visual myth/reveal.

beats.text: Pausing Fabric capacity does not stop the charge for a reservation you already bought.
A reservation discount applies hour by hour. Unused hours do not carry forward.
So check how your reservation benefit is being used before you pause capacity.
There is a second check. Remaining cumulative overages and smoothed operations are added to your Azure bill when you pause.
Use the Capacity Metrics app to inspect the capacity's usage.
Before pausing, check the reservation and pending usage together. A green pause button does not erase an existing commitment.
